chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:

About a man who purchases a sacrificial animal that is one-eyed, but he does not realize it until after buying it: does it suffice for him? He said: “Yes, unless it is a hady, for it is not permissible for it to be deficient.”

key_terms.الضَّحِيَّةَ: the sacrificial animal offered as udhiyah
key_terms.تُجْزِي: suffices or fulfills the required obligation
key_terms.عَوْرَاءَ: one-eyed; having a visible defect in the eye
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering associated with hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Does a one-eyed sacrificial animal count if the defect is discovered only after purchase?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on a sacrificial animal that is discovered to be defective after purchase. It states that such an animal may suffice as an udhiyah, but not as a hady for hajj, since the hady must not be deficient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3059 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)

about a man who purchases a sacrificial animal that is one-eyed, but he only realizes it after buying it. Does it suffice for him?
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, unless it is for a hady (sacrificial offering for Hajj), for it is not permissible for it to be deficient."
